note: Differences between rio-vt and alacritty_terminal that are understood. Each entry says how to take its cause out of a case; a cross-core finding is explained by an entry when removing that cause makes the cores agree (run.py, classify_all). Explained findings are still counted in every summary. An entry is a claim about the cores, so it carries its evidence and, where one core is wrong, the issue that tracks it.

differences.reason: When a pane is resized, rio-vt keeps more rows than alacritty: extra blank rows in history, and a widened line keeps the padding it was wrapped with ("1235      r" against "1235r"). Settled on 2026-10-19 with tmux as a third opinion: in every minimized case checked, tmux agrees with alacritty, and rio-vt agrees too once the text style (bold, dim, italic, underline, reverse) is taken out. So the cause is the same as clear-screen-with-an-attribute: rio-vt counts blank cells written under a style as content, and reflow keeps them. TD resizes panes on every split, so this is user-visible. Not fixable at TD's side of the boundary, for the reason clear-screen-with-an-attribute gives; the fix belongs upstream. The neutralize rule still drops every resize, which is broad; narrow it once the styled-blank fix lands.
differences.evidence: minimized: size 10x3, writes "\x1b[1m", "\x1bM1235", resize 3x2, "r", resize 80x3 -> row rio "1235      r", alacritty and tmux "1235r"; without \x1b[1m rio "1235r". size 4x2, writes "\x1b[2m", "\x1b[J", resize 3x10 -> history rio 1, alacritty 0, tmux 0; without the style rio 0

differences.wrong: neither: TD drops it on purpose
differences.reason: A combining mark or zero-width joiner with nothing to sit on, at the start of a line or after any escape sequence other than a colour: alacritty attaches it (to a blank, or to the last printed character), and under rio-vt TD drops it before the core sees it. That drop is TD's own text guard (vt/text.rs), which lets a mark through only straight after the character it belongs to so that a cursor move cannot walk the per-character mark limit; it is deliberate. tmux 3.7c also drops a mark at the start of a line, so alacritty is the odd one out there.
differences.evidence: minimized: size 4x1, write U+0323 -> row 0 rio "", alacritty " \u0323"; size 2x1, writes "m", "\x1bb", U+200D -> rio "m", alacritty "m\u200d"
differences.third_opinion: tmux 3.7c: a lone U+0323 at column 0 leaves the row empty, as rio-vt under TD does

differences.reason: Erasing characters, a line or the screen (ECH, EL, ED) where the erase covers only one half of a wide character, or the cursor sits on its right half: rio-vt clears the whole character, alacritty can keep it. Split on 2026-10-19 out of one broad entry that removed every wide character from a case, which would have hidden any new wide-character bug: each entry now removes one operation, and only from a case that holds a wide character. Which core is right differs by operation and is not settled; xterm's own behaviour differs by operation too.

differences.reason: A tab leaves a literal tab in the first cell it covers, so copying the line gives the tab back. rio-vt 0.5.28 does that only when the cell is blank (NUL); alacritty and tmux also do it over a space a program wrote there. So after " \r\t" a copy from rio-vt gives a space where the other two give a tab. Not fixable at TD's side of the boundary without wrapping all of rio-vt's handler: the guard cannot see what a cell holds. Copy fidelity only; nothing on screen differs. Fix belongs upstream in put_tab.
differences.evidence: minimized: size 2x1, writes " \r", "\t" -> row 0 rio "", alacritty "\t"
differences.third_opinion: tmux 3.7c: " \r\t" at 2x1 and 4x1 captures as a tab, as alacritty does

differences.reason: rio-vt 0.5.28 erases rows with the cursor's whole style, not just its background (Row::reset takes the template's style id), so a row erased while dim, underline or a foreground colour is set is not empty to it. Clear screen (ED 2) then pushes that row into scrollback, and alacritty and tmux do not. Seen as stray blank lines in scrollback after `clear` under a styled prompt. Not fixable at TD's side of the boundary: every erase and every scroll writes rows this way, so a guard around ED alone would fix half of it. Fix belongs upstream: an erased cell keeps only the background (xterm's bce). The same cause accounts for most of narrowing-reflow.
differences.evidence: minimized: size 4x2, writes "\x1b[2m", "\x1b[J", "\x1b[2J" -> history_size rio 2, alacritty 1; the same without \x1b[2m agrees
differences.third_opinion: tmux 3.7c: "x\e[2m\e[J\e[2J" at 4x2 leaves history_size 1, the same as without \e[2m

differences.reason: When one read completes a UTF-8 character split across reads and also holds more characters after it, vte 0.15.0 prints the completed character but counts the following ones as consumed, so they are never printed. Valid UTF-8 is enough: c3 | a9 61 c3 | a9 62 reads 'ééb' instead of 'éaéb'. rio-vt is not affected. Fixed upstream on vte master, not in any release; only the fallback core (core-alacritty) carries it. Pinned by vt::lab::tests::a_character_split_across_reads_keeps_the_one_after_it.
differences.evidence: minimized by the lab: size 2x1, writes cc | a3 61 88 joined vs whole; root cause advance_partial_utf8 returns valid_bytes - old_bytes after printing only the first character

differences.reason: An incomplete UTF-8 sequence cut short by an escape. Followed by more text, both cores print one replacement character (U+FFFD); left at the end of the input, alacritty prints it at once and rio-vt has not printed it yet. tmux prints nothing at all for it. Found when the wide-character entry was split; seen only from the generator's invalid bytes, never from a real program yet.
differences.evidence: minimized: size 4x2, write "9m" f0 1b, resize to 2x10 -> alacritty shows U+FFFD, rio-vt and tmux do not; f0 1b followed by "x" -> both cores show U+FFFD
